conviction_note: The one growth story that carries this stock - IKE Tech age-gating chips into Charlie's Holdings - was quantified by Ispire's own CEO on 2026-02-06 as 2-3m chips/month showing up in the very quarter now being reported, and the partner's own 2026-09-09 shareholder letter says the launch is still a pilot awaiting IKE's app; four separate negatives sum to about -5, trimmed from the raw -6.7 because findings 1 and 2 share a narrative and because this name has twice popped on forward narrative after a weak print.

findings.finding: Charlie's Holdings' shareholder letter of 2026-09-09 - seven days before Ispire's print - says the age-gated launch is still only a 'pilot test ... this fall' and that shipping waits on Ispire's side ('As soon as IKE's software developers complete their final tests of the consumer app, we will begin shipping'), against Ispire CEO Michael Wang telling the 2026-02-06 call that Charlie's would launch 'in the next two to three months' at 'between 2 million chips a month and 3 million chips a month' and 'we should start seeing results in the next quarter' - i.e. exactly the Apr-Jun fiscal Q4 being reported on 09-16.
findings.why_not_priced: Charlie's is an OTCQB microcap and the letter is a partner-side document that no ISPR wire story references; ISPR's own coverage since March has been the '$50-70 billion flavoured vape TAM' framing with no unit numbers attached. If the market had priced the non-conversion, the posted ISPR consensus for this print would not still be +$0.01 EPS on $21.34m of revenue with a $3.50 mean target against a $1.42 spot - that is a sell-side that has not touched its model since the age-gating narrative began.
findings.independence: Two other documents point the same way and neither is the letter: Charlie's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (Ispire's fiscal Q4) contains no mention of IKE, IKE Tech, Ispire, age-gating or any related licensing agreement anywhere in the filing - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001134765/000143774926028182/chuc20260630_10q.htm ; and Charlie's Q1 2026 release of 2026-05-20 had already pushed the age-gated disposable launch out to 'Q3 2026' from Ispire's February 'two to three months' - https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CHUC/charlie-s-holdings-reports-first-quarter-2026-82dn9fyj78b4.html . Finding 2 below shares the Q2 FY26 transcript with this finding; treat the transcript as one source across the two.

findings.finding: The 'significant development deal around our age-gating technology with a leading global nicotine company in the coming weeks' that Michael Wang promised on the 2026-02-06 call has not been announced in the seven months since: Ispire's own press-release index runs 2026-02-04 to 2026-08-17 with nothing of the kind (the only deal in the gap is the Jincheng Pharma nicotine-pouch JV, a Chinese pharma manufacturing tie-up, not an age-gating licence), and the 2026-05-07 Q3 call did not mention the deal, Charlie's, iQTEC or chip volumes at all.
findings.why_not_priced: A promise that quietly lapses generates no news event and therefore no wire copy - there is nothing for an aggregator to timestamp. If it had been priced, the stock's drift since February would show a discrete gap rather than the slow bleed the baseline records (-9.55% over 20 days, 200-day average $1.71 against a $1.42 spot), and at least one of the three posted analyst ratings would have moved off a $3.50 target.
findings.independence: Ispire's own press-release index, a different source, shows the seven-month gap - https://www.ispiretechnology.com/press-releases (fetched 2026-09-15, listing Feb 4, Mar 11, Mar 16, May 1, May 7, May 12, Aug 17). NOTE: this finding shares the 2026-02-06 Q2 transcript with finding 1 - the shared document is the transcript, and the residual claim here (a named bilateral deal that never appeared) is distinct from the Charlie's launch slip.

findings.finding: Michael Wang - the executive who made both the chip-volume and the 'coming weeks' claims and who ran the growth narrative on the calls - was removed as Co-CEO effective 2026-07-16 and pushed down to running the Aspire North America subsidiary, disclosed in an 8-K carrying Item 5.02 only, with no Item 7.01 and no press release; three weeks later the Przybyla promotion to President got Items 5.02 AND 7.01 plus a PR Newswire release. Tuanfang Liu, the China-based founder-chairman, is now sole CEO.
findings.why_not_priced: The asymmetry is the evidence: the company press-released the promotion and did not press-release the demotion, so the demotion exists only in an EDGAR filing on a $84m name with no option chain and three stale ratings. A general web search for 'Ispire news August 2026' returns the Przybyla appointment and nothing about the CEO change. If it were priced there would be a dated single-day gap in July on the tape and at least one third-party story; neither exists.
findings.independence: The company's own press-release page, a different source, lists the 2026-08-17 Przybyla promotion and no item at all for the 2026-07-16 CEO change - https://www.ispiretechnology.com/press-releases . The contrasting 8-K with Item 7.01 attached is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948455/000121390026090494/ea0302192-8k_ispire.htm (2026-08-17).

findings.finding: Fiscal Q4 is the audited quarter and the receivable book is already 43% reserved: at 2026-03-31 gross accounts receivable were $50,151,620 against an allowance for credit losses of $21,500,062, with $5,564,497 of bad-debt expense in fiscal Q3 alone and $11,537,950 over nine months, while working capital had fallen to roughly $0.8m (current assets $55.7m vs current liabilities $54.9m) from $9.3m two quarters earlier and cash fell from $24.35m to $18.03m.
findings.why_not_priced: The only published estimate for this print is +$0.01 EPS on $21.336m of revenue for a company that lost $0.17 a share on $18.7m of revenue last quarter and $0.69 for FY2025 against a posted 'projected profit of $0.18' - nobody is maintaining a model, so a further year-end provision sits in no one's number. If the provisioning trend were priced, the posted mean target would not be $3.50 on a $1.42 stock. A going-concern paragraph in the FY26 10-K is the tail here and is not in my central case.
findings.independence: The CFO restated the Q3 figure on the 2026-05-07 call ('Credit loss in the quarter was $5.6 million') - https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-ispire-tech-q3-2026-reveals-eps-miss-stock-down-93CH-4668090 . The broken consensus is separately sourced at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-ispire-technology-ispr-expected-to-announce-quarterly-earnings-on-wednesday-2026-09-11/ (2026-09-11).

searched_and_found_nothing: Nasdaq listing compliance - no Item 3.01 8-K and no bid-price or MVLS deficiency notice anywhere in EDGAR; stock is $1.42 and market cap ~$82m, both above the Capital Market thresholds, so the sweep's suggested angle is empty

Dilution / financing overhang - share count is unchanged at 57,399,396 from the 2026-02 10-Q cover through the 2026-05-07 10-Q cover, no ATM, no equity line, no convertible notes, and the only shelf is the 2024-07-29 S-3 with no takedown; this is a mild POSITIVE I could not make into a print-moving finding

Auditor risk - Marcum Asia LLP was ratified for FY2026 at the 2026-06-25 annual meeting with 52.8m for and 2,704 against, so no auditor change, and there was no reverse-split proposal on the ballot (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948455/000121390026072149/ea0295749-8k_ispire.htm)

Insider Form 4 cluster of 2026-08-14 - all three are Code A director stock grants at $0 to Burch, Cox and Fargis 'granted as compensation for services', no open-market buying or selling; no signal either way

IEEPA tariff refunds (struck down by the Supreme Court 2026-02-20) - could not establish that Ispire is importer of record on IEEPA-dutiable goods or that it recognised any refund receivable, and a gain contingency would not be booked anyway; dropped rather than guessed, and it is a correlated exposure across several names
Malaysia regulatory risk - the interim MITI/MIDA nicotine manufacturing licence is export-only and I found no 2026 news of it lapsing, being revoked, or being made final
Litigation - no securities class action or new litigation against Ispire found for 2026 (the Pomerantz item is from 2023-12-05)
FY2026 10-K - not filed as of 2026-09-15 17:15 UTC; last year's was filed 2025-09-15, the day before the call, so it may land before the print and would be the single best source if it does

Reconstructing the four missing earnings reactions (2025-09-16, 2025-11-06, 2026-02-06, 2026-05-07) - could not get clean close-to-close prices for those dates from any reachable source; the only datum is the 2026-05-07 transcript's '6.55% pre-market decline' followed by recovery to +21.74% on the week
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no option chain to agree or disagree with, and my negative lean is partly in the run-up already (-9.55% over 20 days, -61% from the 52-week high), so the honest tension is that I am adding to a direction the tape is already leaning - the part that is genuinely new is the partner-side evidence, dated 2026-09-09 and 2026-06-30, that the age-gating ramp did not happen in the reported quarter and is still a pilot.
